name: Aviddhakarna
dates_notes: Aviddhakarṇa is known through sparse later reports. Neither the date nor the Cārvāka affiliation is secure; the broad early-medieval range records only the relative horizon of the surviving discussion.
evidence_basis: Sparse citations and reports whose interpretation and school affiliation remain disputed.
core_thesis: Aviddhakarṇa is a poorly documented figure cited in discussions of inference. The surviving reports associate him with criticism of formal accounts of inferential validity while allowing that people rely on practical inference in ordinary life. His affiliation is disputed: later classifications have linked the name both to Lokāyata argument and to Nyāya. He therefore belongs in the timeline as a provenance-qualified cited position, not as an unambiguously Cārvāka author or the founder of a distinct school.
